findings.comment:

A CFM must be the person in charge and on duty during all hours of operation when food prep/cooking is taking place.
2-102.12: The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Open packages of roller grill items in the walk in cooler are not date marked with the date of opening. Large packages like the hot dogs and sausages are not used within 24 hours and therefore must be date marked with the date of opening (or alternatively the discard date) and held no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment:
Observed the chili and cheese sauces in the dispenser to be holding at internal temperatures of 111-112F respectively. The thermometer on the unit itself reflects this as well. Pull dispenser from use until unit can be repaired or replaced. Both of these items also had a discard date of 10/28 on them.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding

Do not store PHF in cooler until cooler holds at 41F or below. An order of destruction was filling out for food items that were discarded.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited

Bleach has been used to clean floor drains, and fly strips have been used to catch numerous flies. However, the issue has gotten much worse. At previous inspections only 3-4 flies were observed. Bacon’s is scheduled to come in for service – Management had been advised the PCO cannot get rid of flies. Management needs to work with maintenance crew & owner to locate potential breeding spots – thoroughly clean – and make repairs to areas w/in the cabinets below the soda counter that are damaged. Shelving needs to be removed from the floor inside the cabinets in order to clean gross buildup and work toward eradication of flies. *Owner/management need to contact SCDPH before 10/10/12 if more time is needed to thoroughly clean & make all repairs* *535-3145 ext. 3718 – Allen Alexander, Director of EH*

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Pork eggrolls on the cooker were 95F (surface temp) to 108F (internal temp). Eggrolls had been on the cooker since ~5:30am; however, the eggrolls were not rotating like other products. Also, the temperature of the cooker had been turned down since earlier this morning. All other foods that were on the cooker the same amount of time were at 135F/above. Eggrolls were discarded in the trash. Temperature was turned up on the cooker to continue properly heating foods that were put on after 6am. Maintain hot foods at 135F/above after they have been properly heated to 165F/above. Use calibrated/clean stem thermometer to verify proper temperatures have been reached and are being maintained.
